messages:
jordan (BrightLayer): Hey team — during our CI onboarding run this morning we started seeing a bunch of 429s from the embedding endpoint after the test harness spawns ~40 workers in parallel. Happens within the first 30s of the run.
anya (CS): Sorry you're hitting that — can you paste a small snippet of the failing request/response headers?
jordan (BrightLayer): sure, here's one copy from our logs: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
x-request-id: a1b2c3
authorization: Bearer <ephemeral>
user-agent: bright-ci/1.2.0
--> 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 163
retry-after: 2
```
anya (CS): thanks. Are your workers each fetching their own ephemeral token concurrently or sharing a token?
jordan (BrightLayer): each worker calls our token service at startup — so we get a burst of token refreshes + then immediate embedding calls. we thought ephemeral tokens were cheap, but looks like the preflight/handshake is the hot path.
alex (eng): pinging platform too — this pattern (concurrent token mint + immediate request) will create a short-lived stampede to the auth/preflight layer. We usually recommend splaying token refreshes and caching ephemeral token per process for warmup.
mohit (platform): I can check server-side telemetry — can you share the exact time window? I'll look for connection patterns and whether requests are mapping to multiple regions.
jordan (BrightLayer): sent the window to you via DM mohit — roughly 5523456789 -> 5523456795.
mohit (platform): saw the spike. Most requests came with identical user-agent but unique ephemeral jtis. Edge dropped ~85% of preflight checks into a short window; some upstream retries then hit global concurrency protection and returned 429s.
anya (CS): Actionable short-term mitigations: 1) reduce initial parallelism in the CI harness from 40 -> 8 for warmup, 2) change token logic to reuse a token for the test-run for 30s, 3) implement jittered backoff on 429 with retry-after handling.
jordan (BrightLayer): ok we can flip the harness, but would rather avoid changing test topology. any server-side knobs we can ask for while we roll out client patches?
alex (eng): we can temporarily raise the preflight rate window for your account during onboarding — that buys time. Mohit, can we open a brief rate-window increase for customer brightlayer?
mohit (platform): I can open a 10-minute warmup window to relax concurrent preflight enforcement for that org id. I'll need CS to approve.
anya (CS): I approve for a 10 minute ramp starting once Jordan confirms they're ready. Jordan — tell us when you want the window and we'll flip it.
jordan (BrightLayer): please flip now if you can — we're ready.
deploy-bot: rate-window adjustment applied to org brightlayer for 10m by mohit. ticket=PLAT-9241
alex (eng): Client guidance snippet you can paste into your harness: 
```
// reuse token for process
const token = await fetchToken();
await Promise.all(workers.map(async w => {
  await sleep(Math.random() * 200); // splay start
  // use same token for first 30s
  return callEmbedding({ token });
}));
// backoff on 429
if (res.status === 429) {
  await sleep( (2 ** retry) * 100 + jitter() );
}
```
anya (CS): Also set your token TTL cache to 30s and add small random start delays for parallel jobs. That combination almost always fixes onboarding stampedes.
jordan (BrightLayer): deployed the client patch (reused token + splay + backoff). re-running now.
jordan (BrightLayer): quick update — catch rate is much better already. we still saw a couple of 429s early but they recovered. thanks for the warmup window.
mohit (platform): telemetry shows the cold spike is now smoothed, preflight failures down to <5%. I'll close the temporary window in ~5m.
anya (CS): excellent — I'll follow up with onboarding notes for your account (recommended warmup flags + sample harness snippet) and add to our onboarding checklist. anything else?
jordan (BrightLayer): could you also share expected best practices for ephemeral token refresh cadence? we want a short doc to give engineering.
anya (CS): yep — I'll post a short doc in the onboarding repo: suggested defaults: reuse token per process 15–60s, splay starts, handle 429 with exponential backoff + jitter, and request temporary warmup windows for big CI bursts.
jordan (BrightLayer): perfect, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
anya (CS): follow-up: created onboarding note PR and notified renewals team about smoother ramp. closing thread after mohit flips window back.
mohit (platform): window expired, reverted to normal enforcement. all good.
jordan (BrightLayer): all green on our side — thanks again.
